items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Mr. Taukman' only in response to the interviewer's prompt ('I heard Ben, Mr. Taukman.') and does not provide any personal interaction, relationship, or narrative involving Mr. Taukman.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. She rode the horse bareback, I think, with just the flannel over to keep her dress clean, but she was always beautifully gowned. And these pigeons made a perfect pitch out of her, because she was a beautiful woman in those days. And Mr. Jones and the circus would so acclaim her. And with these pigeons, the white pigeons, you know, with a little streak in the wings, lighting on her shoulder, she made a picture, a picture that you couldn't resist looking at. And these were flashing on the billboards, see?…

Uh-huh. And the Cole Brothers Circus was playing there as a special attraction, and Miles has 15 pieces in his band. But I'm Miles' bandmaster, because Miles liked to play the drums to keep the tempo out. So I have to take over for Miles. That's Joel Morris playing there also. And the little Jap Loveless, he's there. And then is when I had to really cut it, because the bulk of the work was on me, playing all of these gallops and fast marches and sailing from one number to another, you know.
